findings: CORS wildcard in server/index.js (Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *) is appropriate for local dev but must be restricted before any production or patient-data deployment. The code carries a comment acknowledging this — no action needed now, but it should be on the pre-production checklist.

auth.js uses plain string equality for API key comparison, which is vulnerable to timing attacks. The 'SECURITY REVIEW REQUIRED' comment already flags this; a production version should use crypto.timingSafeEqual. Non-blocking for a prototype.
server/index.js readBody has no body-size cap, allowing a large-payload DoS against a deployed instance. Non-blocking for a prototype; add a limit before any network-exposed deployment.

Scripts were placed in genomex-final/api/ (per FEAT-002 spec) rather than scripts/ as referenced in the review prompt. Both batch_evaluate.js and synthetic_demo.js are present, use fileURLToPath, and satisfy all script-level hard constraints — the path discrepancy is in the review prompt, not in the implementation.
summary: All 9 hard constraints pass: no numeric score fields in server responses or script output (confirmed by code and test), auth.js and audit.js carry required security/PHI comments, research-panel.js uses only h() with no innerHTML, model predictions are not wired into rule categories, all path resolutions use fileURLToPath(new URL(...)), synthetic_demo prints SYNTHETIC DATA banner and monitor gap note, helpers.js Windows path fix is in place, and engine/ was not modified. Server tests cover all 6 required cases. DISCLAIMER and ClinPGx CC BY-SA 4.0 attribution are sourced from engine/report.js constants. The four findings are informational notes about production-hardening concerns; none are blocking for a prototype.
